mainTopic: Changes to the ברכות during the Ten Days, teachings of רב about prayer and shame, the sections of קריאת שמע, and mentioning יציאת מצרים at night.
overview: The גמרא opens by describing how רב ששת bowed quickly and stood up slowly. רבה בר חיננא סבא, in the name of רב, then teaches that during the ten days from ראש השנה to יום כיפור we say 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט'. רבי אלעזר disagrees, but the הלכה follows רבה, who agrees with רב. More teachings in רב's name follow: whoever can pray for another person and does not is called a sinner, and a תלמיד חכם deserves even more worry. Another teaching says that whoever is ashamed of a sin is forgiven for all his sins, and this is proven from שאול. The גמרא then explains why the חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע but did not, and why פרשת ציצית was included. A new משנה rules that יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night, based on בן זומא's reading of 'all the days of your life'. The חכמים read that same פסוק as including the days of the משיח, and the גמרא brings their debate with בן זומא, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How רב ששת bowed and stood up
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת bowed down quickly, all at once, and stood back up slowly.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב ששת bowed, he bowed like a cane. When he stood up, he stood up like a snake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how רב ששת himself bowed during prayer. He went down in one quick motion and came back up slowly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cane snaps straight down in one motion, so his bow was quick and complete. A snake lifts its head first and slowly raises the rest of its body, so his rising was gradual. This shows how a person bows with awe of ה׳.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a cane or stick, meaning all at once.
He straightens up or stands upright.
Like a snake, meaning slowly, head first.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet, when he bowed,
bowed like a cane.
phrases.notes: Picture a stick dropping straight down. He went down in one quick motion.

phrases.english: When he would stand up,
he stood up like a snake.
phrases.notes: A snake lifts its head first and slowly raises the rest of its body.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב שֵׁשֶׁת, כִּי כָּרַע — כָּרַע כְּחִיזְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the דף about how to bow during prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bow quickly and completely, and rise slowly.

steps.title: Changing two blessing endings during the Ten Days
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא in the name of רב: from ראש השנה to יום כיפור we switch 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' to 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט' to 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: All year a person prays 'the holy God' and 'King who loves righteousness and justice.' The exception is the ten days between ראש השנה and יום כיפור, when he prays 'the holy King' and 'the King of justice.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב rules that during the ten days from ראש השנה to יום כיפור, two ברכות in שמונה עשרה end with different wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year-round endings are 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' in the third ברכה and 'מֶלֶךְ אוֹהֵב צְדָקָה וּמִשְׁפָּט' in the ברכה about judges. In these ten days ה׳ is shown as King and Judge in a special way, so both endings switch to stress 'הַמֶּלֶךְ'.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy God, the usual ending of the third ברכה.
King who loves righteousness and justice, the usual ending of the ברכה about judges.
The holy King, said during the Ten Days.
The King of justice, the King who shows Himself through judgment.
The ten days from ראש השנה through יום כיפור.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the familiar practice of saying 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט' during עשרת ימי תשובה.

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Chinnana the Elder said
in the name of Rav:
All year long
a person prays 'The holy God,'
phrases.notes: This is how the third ברכה of שמונה עשרה ends.

phrases.english: and 'King who loves righteousness and justice,'
phrases.notes: This is the ending of the ברכה that asks ה׳ to bring back our judges.

phrases.english: except for the ten days
between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur,
when he prays 'The holy King'
and 'The King of justice.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from how to bow to a new topic: the wording of ברכות during the Ten Days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During the ten days from ראש השנה to יום כיפור, end with 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר says the usual wording is acceptable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rules that even someone who said 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' during the Ten Days has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: even if he said 'the holy God,' he has fulfilled his obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב. He says the regular ending 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' still works even during the Ten Days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the wording changes in these days. רבי אלעזר says changing it is not required, because the regular wording already does the job. His proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He has fulfilled his obligation and does not need to repeat.

phrases.english: But Rabbi Elazar said:
Even if he said 'The holy God,'
he has fulfilled his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ אָמַר הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to רב's ruling in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' during the Ten Days is acceptable.

steps.title: Proof from a פסוק in ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק that speaks of ה׳'s judgment, which fits the Ten Days, and that same פסוק still calls Him 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ'.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And ה׳ of hosts is exalted through justice, and the holy God is made holy through righteousness.' When is ה׳ 'exalted through justice'? In the ten days from ראש השנה until יום כיפור. Yet the verse says 'the holy God.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר proves his view from a פסוק. A verse about ה׳ as Judge, which fits the Ten Days, still calls Him 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the פסוק describes the time of judgment, which he identifies as the Ten Days. The second half, about that very time, uses 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and not 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ'. So the regular wording is fitting even then.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says, introducing a פסוק.
And He is exalted, raised high.

steps.confusionAlert: The question 'אֵימָתַי' is not a challenge from someone else. It explains how רבי אלעזר's פסוק proves his point (it may be the גמרא's explanation rather than his own words), showing which days the פסוק is talking about.

phrases.english: As it says: 'And ה׳ of hosts is exalted through justice,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 5:16

phrases.english: and the holy God is made holy through righteousness.'
When is 'ה׳ of hosts exalted through justice'?
These are the ten days
from Rosh Hashanah until Yom Kippur,
and yet it says 'The holy God.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיִּגְבַּה ה׳ צְבָאוֹת בַּמִּשְׁפָּט וְהָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ נִקְדָּשׁ בִּצְדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's ruling that 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' is acceptable during the Ten Days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 5:16: its first half describes the time of judgment, the Ten Days, and its second half still says 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ'.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion the הלכה follows, רב or רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the practical bottom line between רב and רבי אלעזר. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now have two opinions: רב requires the change in wording, and רבי אלעזר says the usual wording is fine. The גמרא wants to know which one we follow in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: What was concluded about it? A request for the final הלכה.

steps.whatToRemember: רב says to switch to 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט' during the Ten Days. רבי אלעזר says 'הָאֵל הַקָּדוֹשׁ' still works, based on ישעיהו 5:16. The גמרא is about to decide between them.

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both opinions are presented, asks for the practical ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the הלכה follows רב (change the wording) or רבי אלעזר (the usual wording is acceptable).

steps.title: רב יוסף and רבה carry on the same argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says to keep the regular wording all year. רבה says to switch to 'King' wording during the Ten Days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: we say 'the holy God' and 'King Who loves righteousness and justice.' רבה said: we say 'the holy King' and 'the King of justice.'
steps.whatsHappening: To answer 'which way is the הלכה?', the גמרא first shows that two later אמוראים argued about the very same point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף keeps the regular wording, matching רבי אלעזר. רבה uses the 'King' wording, matching רב. This step lines up the two sides so the גמרא can now decide between them.

keyTerms.meaning: Righteousness and justice (the year-round ending of the blessing)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
'The holy God'
and 'King Who loves righteousness and justice.'
phrases.notes: He means: keep the regular year-round wording, even during the Ten Days.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
'The holy King'
and 'The King of justice.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 5 by showing the argument continued among later אמוראים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument between רב and רבי אלעזר continues: רב יוסף agrees with רבי אלעזר, and רבה agrees with רב.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules like רבה: during the Ten Days we say 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final answer: we follow רבה, and that means we follow רב's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the question from step 5. Even though רבי אלעזר brought a פסוק, the practical ruling is to switch to the 'King' wording during the Ten Days.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה (the practical ruling) is

steps.whatToRemember: During the Ten Days from ראש השנה to יום כיפור, we say 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ' and 'הַמֶּלֶךְ הַמִּשְׁפָּט', as רבה ruled following רב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source of the Ten Days changes in the שמונה עשרה that people still say today.

phrases.english: And the halakha is like Rabba.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute laid out in step 6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה is like רבה: switch to the 'King' wording during the Ten Days.

steps.title: Not praying for someone else is called sinning
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא, in the name of רב, teaches that anyone who could pray for another person and does not is called a sinner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: anyone who is able to ask for mercy for his friend and does not ask is called a 'sinner.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from the same speaker as step 2: if you can pray for another person, you must.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic moves from wording to a duty. Choosing not to pray for someone you could help is not just a missed chance. It is labeled a sin.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask for mercy (to pray for someone)

phrases.english: And Rabba bar Ḥinnana Sava said
in the name of Rav:
Anyone who is able
to ask for mercy on behalf of his friend
and does not ask
is called a 'sinner.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same speaker as step 2, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who could pray for another person and does not is called a sinner.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל's words
steps.stepSummary: שמואל הנביא says it would be a sin against ה׳ for him to stop praying for the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Also I, far be it from me to sin against ה׳ by stopping to pray for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the teaching in step 8: a פסוק where שמואל calls not praying a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל connects 'sinning against ה׳' directly with 'stopping to pray for you.' That is exactly why someone who does not pray is called a חוטא.

phrases.english: As it is stated:
'Also I, far be it from me
phrases.notes: שמואל א 12:23

phrases.english: to sin against the Lord
by stopping to pray for you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 8 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That not praying for another person is called a sin
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 12:23: שמואל calls stopping to pray a sin against ה׳.

steps.title: For a Torah scholar you must worry until it makes you ill
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds that when the person in need is a תלמיד חכם, just praying is not enough. You must worry about him until it makes you ill.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: if he is a תלמיד חכם, one needs to make himself ill over him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises the level of the duty when the person who needs mercy is a תלמיד חכם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 required prayer for anyone. רבא says a תלמיד חכם deserves more: you should be so worried and pained that it affects your own health.

keyTerms.meaning: That he make himself ill (from worry)

phrases.english: Rava said:
If he is a Torah scholar,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person who needs the mercy, the one being prayed for.

phrases.english: one must make himself ill over him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8, adding a stronger duty for a תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a תלמיד חכם, one must worry so much that he makes himself ill.

steps.title: What is the source for רבא's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבא learned that you must make yourself ill over a תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רבא's teaching. This sets up the next steps, where it tries out possible proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's rule is a strong demand. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? (Where is it learned from?)

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in a פסוק for making oneself ill over a תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: Suggested proof from King שאול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a proof from שאול, who complained that none of his men were ill over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you will say it is because it is written: 'And none of you is ill over me, and none tells it to me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a first possible source: שאול complaining that nobody was pained over him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול complains that no one 'became ill' over him, which suggests they should have. The word אילימא warns us this proof is about to be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (a suggestion that usually gets rejected)
Reveals to my ear, tells me

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written:
'And none of you is ill over me
phrases.notes: שמואל א 22:8

phrases.english: and none tells it to me' —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That one must make himself ill over a תלמיד חכם
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 22:8: שאול complains that no one was ill over him.

steps.title: Maybe a king is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from שאול: a king might deserve extra worry, so we cannot learn from him about every תלמיד חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a king is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the suggested proof from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שאול was a king. People may need to worry this much about a king because of his position, and that does not prove the same for an ordinary תלמיד חכם.

phrases.english: Perhaps a king is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from שאול, not רבא's rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case involves a king, who may be special, so it cannot be applied to every תלמיד חכם.

steps.title: The real proof from דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a better source: דוד says that when others were sick, he wore sackcloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn it from here: 'And I, when they were sick, my clothing was sackcloth, and so on.'
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the proof from שאול, the גמרא gives the proof it accepts, from a פסוק of דוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here דוד himself is the one worrying. He wore sackcloth when others were sick, so there is no 'king' problem on the side of the person being prayed for. This shows how deeply one should feel the pain of a sick תלמיד חכם.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (bringing a better source)

steps.whatToRemember: We must pray for anyone we can help. For a תלמיד חכם, we must feel real pain over him, as דוד did, not just say a quick prayer.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
'And I, when they were sick, my clothing, etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 35:13. The פסוק goes on: 'was sackcloth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected proof of step 12 with an accepted source.
steps.raayaObject: That one must make himself ill over a תלמיד חכם
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 35:13: דוד wore sackcloth when others were sick.

steps.title: Being ashamed of a sin brings full forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר חיננא סבא says in the name of רב that anyone who sins and is ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר חיננא סבא said in the name of רב: anyone who does a sin and is ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching: feeling real shame over a sin earns forgiveness for all of one's sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a fresh statement linked to the earlier ones by 'and he said.' It says shame alone has great power: it brings forgiveness for everything, not only for the one sin.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar Chinnana the Elder said in the name of Rav:
Anyone who does a sinful act
and is ashamed of it,
they forgive him for all his sins.
phrases.notes: 'They' here means Heaven. ה׳ forgives him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר חִינָּנָא סָבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same chain of sayings, not tied to the previous proof about דוד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who sins and is ashamed of it is forgiven for all his sins.

steps.title: A פסוק in יחזקאל links shame to forgiveness
steps.stepSummary: The source is a פסוק where ה׳ says the people will remember, feel ashamed, and be forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'So that you remember and be ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your shame, when I forgive you for all you have done, says ה׳ God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for the teaching that shame brings forgiveness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, shame ('וָבֹשְׁתְּ', 'כְּלִמָּתֵךְ') appears right next to ה׳ forgiving 'all that you did.' That matches the teaching: shame leads to forgiveness for everything.

keyTerms.meaning: An opening of the mouth; an excuse or a reason to speak

phrases.english: As it says: "So that you remember and be ashamed,
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 16:63

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא יִהְיֶה לָּךְ עוֹד פִּתְחוֹן פֶּה
phrases.english: and you will no longer have an opening of the mouth
because of your shame,
when I forgive you for all that you have done,
says ה׳ God."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the teaching in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: Shame over sin brings forgiveness for all sins.

steps.title: Maybe a community is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes off the proof: the פסוק speaks to the whole people, and a community may be forgiven more easily than one person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps a community is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from יחזקאל, because that פסוק may only work for a whole community.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to the whole nation. A צבור might get forgiveness more easily, so we cannot prove that a single person who feels ashamed is also forgiven.

phrases.english: Perhaps a community is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from יחזקאל, not the teaching itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about a צבור, which may be forgiven more easily than an individual.

steps.title: A new proof: שאול did not mention the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a proof about one person, שאול. When he speaks to שמואל, he mentions the prophets and dreams but not the אורים ותומים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the proof is from here: 'And שמואל said to שאול: Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up? And שאול said: I am in great trouble. The Philistines are fighting me, and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me, not through the prophets and not through dreams. So I called you to tell me what to do.' But he did not mention the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new proof, this time about a single person, שאול. It points out that he left the אורים ותומים off his list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the proof is about one person, so the problem of 'a community is different' goes away. The key is what שאול leaves out: he names prophets and dreams but not the אורים ותומים. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, from here (bringing a better source)
The כהן גדול's breastplate, used to ask ה׳ questions

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not in what שאול says. It is in what he does not say: he leaves out the אורים ותומים.

phrases.english: Rather, from here:
"And Samuel said to Saul:
phrases.notes: שמואל א 28:15

phrases.english: Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?
And Saul said: I am in great distress,
and the Philistines are fighting against me,

phrases.aramaic: וַה׳ סָר מֵעָלַי וְלֹא עָנָנִי עוֹד
phrases.english: and God has turned away from me and no longer answers me,
neither through the prophets nor through dreams;
so I have called you to tell me what I should do."
But the "Urim and Tummim" he did not mention.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the proof that was pushed off in step 17 with one about a single person.
steps.raayaObject: A single person who is ashamed of his sin is forgiven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 28:15, and what שאול leaves out of his words

steps.title: Why שאול left out the אורים ותומים
steps.stepSummary: שאול did not mention the אורים ותומים because he had killed נוב, the city of the כהנים. He was ashamed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he had killed the people of נוב, the city of the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שאול left out the אורים ותומים: he had killed the כהנים of נוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אורים ותומים was used through a כהן. After destroying the city of the כהנים, שאול was too ashamed to mention it. This shows that שאול felt shame over his sin.

keyTerms.meaning: נוב, the city of the כהנים

phrases.english: Because he had killed the people of Nov, the city of the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the silence noticed in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שאול left out the אורים ותומים out of shame, because he had killed the כהנים of נוב.
steps.raayaObject: That שאול was ashamed of his sin, the first half of the proof for step 15.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שאול's silence about the אורים ותומים (שמואל א 28:15), explained by his killing the כהנים of נוב.

steps.title: How do we know שאול was forgiven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for proof that Heaven really forgave שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that he was forgiven by Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the last piece of the proof by asking how we know שאול was forgiven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we have only shown that שאול was ashamed. To prove רב's teaching, we also need to show that the shame brought forgiveness. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he was forgiven by Heaven?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second half of the proof: forgiveness, not just shame.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that שאול's shame actually led Heaven to forgive him.

steps.title: 'With me' means in שמואל's place
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells שאול, 'Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me.' רבי יוחנן explains that 'with me' means in my place, so שאול was forgiven.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And שמואל said to שאול: Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me.' And רבי יוחנן said: 'With me' means in my section.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves שאול was forgiven: שמואל says שאול will be 'with me,' and רבי יוחנן reads that as being in שמואל's own place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With me' does not only mean שאול will die. It means he will be in the same place as שמואל, a צדיק. That could only happen if he was forgiven. So shame brought forgiveness, and רב's teaching is proven for a single person.

keyTerms.meaning: In my section, in my company

steps.whatToRemember: One who sins and is truly ashamed is forgiven for all his sins. The proof is שאול: he was too ashamed to mention the אורים ותומים after killing the כהנים of נוב, and שמואל told him he would be 'with me,' meaning in the place of the צדיקים.

phrases.english: As it says: "And Samuel said to Saul:
phrases.notes: שמואל א 28:19

phrases.english: and tomorrow you and your sons will be with me."
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'מחר' and some say 'ומחר'; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
"With me" means in my section.
phrases.notes: He means שאול will be in the same place as שמואל, not just that he will die.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וַיֹּאמֶר שְׁמוּאֵל אֶל שָׁאוּל וּמָחָר אַתָּה וּבָנֶיךָ עִמִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20 and finishes the proof for step 15.
steps.raayaObject: Heaven forgave שאול, so shame brings forgiveness even for one person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל א 28:19, as explained by רבי יוחנן
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A single person who is ashamed of his sin is forgiven, as shown by שאול.

steps.title: The רבנן bring a different proof that Heaven forgave שאול
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן prove שאול was forgiven from a פסוק that calls him 'the chosen of ה׳'. They explain that these words were said by a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן say the proof comes from here: 'And we will hang them up to ה׳ in the גבעה of שאול, the chosen of ה׳.' A בת קול came out and said, 'the chosen of ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a second proof, different from רבי יוחנן's proof, that Heaven forgave שאול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The people speaking in this פסוק wanted to punish שאול's family, so they would not praise him. The words 'the chosen of ה׳' must therefore come from a בת קול. If Heaven itself calls שאול 'chosen', he must have been forgiven.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis, the majority of the חכמים
From here, meaning from this source
And we will hang them up

steps.whatToRemember: There are two proofs that שאול was forgiven. רבי יוחנן learns it from 'with me' in שמואל's words. The רבנן learn it from the בת קול that called him 'the chosen of ה׳'.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say: from here
"And we will hang them up to ה׳
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 21:6

phrases.english: in the Giva of Shaul, the chosen of ה׳."
A heavenly voice came out
and said, "the chosen of ה׳."
phrases.notes: The גמרא means the people in the פסוק did not say these last words. Heaven added them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source from רבי יוחנן's proof in Step 21 that שאול was forgiven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל ב 21:6, 'בחיר ה׳', read as spoken by a בת קול
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the side discussion about whether one person can be forgiven, which began back in Step 17.

steps.title: The חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע but did not
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע. They held back so the people would not be overburdened.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו בן זוטרתי said in the name of רבי יהודה בר זבידא: They wanted to set פרשת בלק into קריאת שמע. Why did they not set it? Because it would be a burden on the congregation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic of the chapter, קריאת שמע, and brings a new statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים saw something valuable in פרשת בלק and wanted it in the daily שמע. They decided against it because the section is long. Making everyone say it twice a day would be too heavy.

keyTerms.meaning: To set in place as a fixed part
The section about בלק and בלעם's blessings

phrases.english: Rabbi Abahu ben Zutarti said
Rabbi Yehuda bar Zevida said:
They wanted to establish the portion of Balak
in the reading of Shema,
and why did they not establish it?
Because of the burden on the congregation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בֶּן זוּטַרְתִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר זְבִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of שאול and returns to קריאת שמע with a new statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים wanted to add פרשת בלק to קריאת שמע but did not, because of טורח צבור.

steps.title: Why did they want to add it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was special about פרשת בלק that made the חכמים want to add it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next steps: what made פרשת בלק fit for שמע?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 told us why it was left out, but not why it was wanted. The גמרא now looks for the positive reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why did they want to add פרשת בלק in the first place?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the wish described in Step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What feature of פרשת בלק made it a candidate for קריאת שמע

steps.title: Mentioning יציאת מצרים cannot be the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is that פרשת בלק mentions יציאת מצרים. It rejects this, because short sections like פרשת רבית and פרשת משקלות mention it too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it is written there, 'God who brings them out of מצרים', then let us say פרשת רבית and פרשת משקלות, where יציאת מצרים is also written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out one possible reason and immediately knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goal were only to mention יציאת מצרים, the חכמים could have picked shorter sections that also mention it. Those would not be a burden. So there must be something else special about פרשת בלק.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
The Torah section about lending with interest
The Torah section about honest weights

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's answer. אילימא brings up an idea only to push it away. The real answer comes next with אלא.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it is written in it:
"God who brings them out of Egypt"
phrases.notes: במדבר 23:22

phrases.english: then let us say the portion of interest
and the portion of weights
in which the going out of Egypt is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to Step 24's question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that mentioning יציאת מצרים is why פרשת בלק was chosen
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other sections mention יציאת מצרים too, so this reason does not single out פרשת בלק.

steps.title: The real reason: a פסוק about lying down and rising
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין says the reason is a פסוק in פרשת בלק about crouching, lying down, and being raised up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוסי בר אבין said: it is because this פסוק is written there: 'He crouched, he lay down like a lion, and like a lioness, who will raise him up?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer to why the חכמים wanted פרשת בלק in שמע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק talks about lying down and getting up, just like שמע says 'when you lie down and when you rise'. Only פרשת בלק has this match, so it was the one they wanted to add.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים wanted פרשת בלק in שמע because of 'כרע שכב... מי יקימנו', which matches 'בשכבך ובקומך'. They left it out only because it was too long for the people.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין,
phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
because this verse is written in it:
"He crouched, he lay down like a lion
and like a lioness, who will raise him up?"
phrases.notes: במדבר 24:9. Lying down and rising up echo שמע's 'בשכבך ובקומך'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason from Step 25 with the real reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרשת בלק contains 'כרע שכב כארי... מי יקימנו', which parallels lying down and rising in שמע.

steps.title: Why not say just that one פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: If the only reason to add פרשת בלק is one פסוק, the גמרא asks why we don't just say that פסוק by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let us say this one פסוק and nothing more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of רבי יוסי בר אבין. If one פסוק is the whole point, just add that one פסוק and skip the rest of the long section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23 the חכמים held back from adding פרשת בלק because it is too long a burden for the people. But if only one פסוק matters, the length problem disappears: say only that פסוק. So why didn't they?

phrases.english: And let him say this verse
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק from step 26, about crouching, lying down, and being raised up.

phrases.english: and nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges what follows from the answer in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the חכמים had to choose between the whole of פרשת בלק and nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one פסוק is the key, saying only that פסוק avoids burdening the people, so the חכמים had no reason to hold back.

steps.title: We only break where משה רבינו broke
steps.stepSummary: There is a tradition that we may only cut a section where משה רבינו made a break. So we cannot pull out one פסוק by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have a tradition: any section that משה רבינו broke off, we may break off. A section that משה רבינו did not break off, we may not break off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a tradition. We are not allowed to cut the תורה into pieces wherever we like, only at the places where משה רבינו himself made a break.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about crouching is in the middle of a section, not at a break made by משה רבינו. So it cannot be read alone. The only choices were the whole long section or nothing, and the חכמים chose not to burden the people.
steps.whatToRemember: We may only break off a piece of the תורה at a place where משה רבינו made a break. That is why the פסוק from פרשת בלק could not be said alone.

phrases.english: We have a tradition: any section
that Moshe our teacher broke off, we break off,

phrases.aramaic: דְּלָא פַּסְקַהּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ — לָא פָּסְקִינַן.
phrases.english: that Moshe our teacher did not break off, we do not break off.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמִירִי: כֹּל פָּרָשָׁה דְּפַסְקַהּ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a rule from tradition that rules out the suggested idea.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One could simply pull out the important פסוק and say it alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסוק cannot be cut out where משה רבינו made no break, so it was all of פרשת בלק or nothing.

steps.title: Why was פרשת ציצית chosen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why פרשת ציצית was made a set part of קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why did they set פרשת ציצית as part of קריאת שמע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question about the third section of קריאת שמע. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as the גמרא asked what was special about פרשת בלק, it now asks what is special about פרשת ציצית. The answer should explain what it adds that earned it a fixed place.

keyTerms.meaning: They set it / made it fixed

phrases.english: The section of tzitzis, for what reason did they set it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 24, now about a different section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is special about פרשת ציצית that made the חכמים put it into קריאת שמע.

steps.title: פרשת ציצית holds a list of key topics
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר חביבא says פרשת ציצית was set because it contains a list of important topics.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר חביבא said: Because it has five things in it: the מצוה of ציצית, leaving מצרים, the yoke of the מצוות, the thinking of heretics, thoughts of sin, and thoughts of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה בר חביבא answers the question. פרשת ציצית earned its place because so many important topics are packed into it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the single פסוק of פרשת בלק, פרשת ציצית is a short section that can be read whole. It contains the מצוה of ציצית, the memory of leaving מצרים, accepting the מצוות, and warnings against wrong beliefs and sinful thoughts.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא says 'five things' but the list has six. Some explain that יציאת מצרים, the main reason, is not counted in the five. Don't let the count throw you.
steps.whatToRemember: פרשת ציצית is in קריאת שמע because it holds many key topics, including יציאת מצרים and warnings against sinful thoughts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Chaviva said,
because it has five things in it:
the מצוה of tzitzis, leaving Egypt,
the yoke of the מצוות, and the thinking of heretics,
phrases.notes: The section warns against these: 'do not stray after your heart and your eyes.'

phrases.english: thoughts of sin, and thoughts of idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר חֲבִיבָא, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פרשת ציצית was set because it holds a list of key topics: ציצית, יציאת מצרים, עול מצוות, and warnings against heresy, sinful thoughts, and עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Three topics are clear, but where are the other three?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the yoke of מצוות, ציצית, and יציאת מצרים are written openly in פרשת ציצית. It then asks where heresy, sinful thoughts, and thoughts of עבודה זרה are found.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, three of the topics are written clearly: the yoke of מצוות, ציצית, and leaving Egypt each have a פסוק. But where do we see heresy, sinful thoughts, and thoughts of idol worship?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks רבי יהודה בר חביבא's list from step 30. Three items are easy to find, so it asks where the other three come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words בשלמא and אלא set up a contrast: the first part is accepted, and the second part is under pressure. If three of the topics cannot be found in the פרשה, his reason for including it would be weaker. So the גמרא needs a source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / fine (accepts one part before challenging another)
The yoke of the מצוות, accepting all the commandments
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: Granted, these three are stated explicitly.
The yoke of מצוות, as it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וּרְאִיתֶם אֹתוֹ וּזְכַרְתֶּם אֶת כָּל מִצְוֹת ה׳״.
phrases.english: "And you shall see it and remember all the מצוות of ה׳."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:39

phrases.english: Tzitzit, as it is written: "And they shall make for themselves tzitzit, etc."
The Exodus from Egypt, as it is written: "Who took you out, etc."
But the views of heretics,
phrases.notes: These are the other three items from רבי יהודה בר חביבא's list in the step before.

phrases.aramaic: הִרְהוּר עֲבֵירָה, וְהִרְהוּר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה — מְנָלַן?
phrases.english: sinful thoughts, and thoughts of idol worship: from where do we know them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the list of topics given in step 30
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה בר חביבא's claim that פרשת ציצית contains all six topics
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only three of the six topics are openly written in the פרשה, so the source for the other three is unclear

steps.title: A ברייתא finds the other three topics in the words of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'after your hearts' as heresy, 'after your eyes' as sinful thoughts, and 'you stray' as thoughts of עבודה זרה. Each reading is backed by another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: 'After your hearts' means heresy, like 'The fool said in his heart, there is no God.' 'After your eyes' means sinful thoughts, like שמשון saying 'take her for me, for she is right in my eyes.' 'You stray' means thoughts of idol worship, like 'they strayed after the בעלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. It shows that the missing three topics are hinted in three phrases of one פסוק in פרשת ציצית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase is linked to its topic through another פסוק that uses the same kind of word. 'Heart' is tied to the fool who denies God in his heart. 'Eyes' is tied to שמשון wanting a woman he saw. 'Straying' is tied to Israel chasing the בעלים. Now all six topics are found in the פרשה.

keyTerms.meaning: Straying, being unfaithful (here, a picture of idol worship)
And so it says (brings a supporting פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: פרשת ציצית holds six topics: the yoke of מצוות, ציצית, and יציאת מצרים are said openly. Heresy, sinful thoughts, and עבודה זרה are hinted in 'after your hearts, after your eyes, you stray.'

phrases.english: As it was taught: "After your hearts"

steps.title: The משנה: יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says that even at about seventy he could not prove it, until בן זומא learned it from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: We mention leaving Egypt at night. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said: I am like a seventy-year-old man, and I never managed to get leaving Egypt said at night, until בן זומא explained it from a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It gives a rule about saying יציאת מצרים at night and tells a short story from רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The third paragraph of קריאת שמע, פרשת ציצית, ends with leaving Egypt. Since ציצית is a daytime מצוה, one might think this paragraph does not belong at night. The משנה rules that we still mention יציאת מצרים at night, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says he could not prove this until בן זומא found a source.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not merit / I did not succeed
He explained it from a פסוק

phrases.english: MISHNA: We mention the Exodus from Egypt at night.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said:
I am like a seventy-year-old man,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זָכִיתִי שֶׁתֵּאָמֵר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם בַּלֵּילוֹת,
phrases.english: and I did not merit that the Exodus from Egypt be said at night,
phrases.notes: He means he could never win the argument and prove that it must be said at night.

phrases.english: until Ben Zoma explained it from a verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of פרשת ציצית ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יציאת מצרים is mentioned at night as well as by day

steps.title: בן זומא's proof: the extra word כל adds the nights
steps.stepSummary: בן זומא quotes 'so that you remember the day you left Egypt all the days of your life.' 'The days of your life' means days, and the extra word 'all' adds nights.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'So that you will remember the day you left Egypt all the days of your life.' 'The days of your life' means the daytime. 'All the days of your life' adds the nights.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives בן זומא's proof from a פסוק. This is the source that settled the question for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have said just 'the days of your life,' and that would mean daytime only. The extra word 'all' must be teaching something more. בן זומא says it adds the nights, so we remember leaving Egypt at night too.

keyTerms.meaning: All the days of your life

steps.whatToRemember: בן זומא learns from the extra word כל in 'all the days of your life' that we mention יציאת מצרים at night too.

phrases.english: As it says: "So that you will remember the day you went out
from the land of Egypt all the days of your life."
phrases.notes: דברים 16:3

phrases.english: "The days of your life": the days,
"All the days of your life": the nights.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לְמַעַן תִּזְכֹּר אֶת יוֹם צֵאתְךָ מֵאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם כֹּל יְמֵי חַיֶּיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק and the reading that בן זומא used, mentioned in step 33
steps.raayaObject: That יציאת מצרים must be mentioned at night
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 16:3, reading the extra word כל as adding the nights

steps.title: The חכמים read 'all' as including the days of the משיח
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say 'the days of your life' means this world, and the extra word 'all' adds the days of the משיח.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: 'The days of your life' means this world. 'All' comes to include the days of the משיח.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the חכמים' reading of the same פסוק בן זומא used. They use the extra word 'all' for something different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן זומא used 'all' to add nights, which is why he says we mention יציאת מצרים at night. The חכמים use 'all' to add a future time, the days of the משיח. So for them this פסוק says nothing about nights.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, to bring in something extra
The days of the משיח, the future redemption

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that the word 'all' adds something. They only disagree about what it adds: nights (בן זומא) or the days of the משיח (חכמים).

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
"The days of your life" means this world.
"All" comes to include the days of the Messiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים' different reading of the same פסוק בן זומא used in step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'All the days of your life' includes this world and the days of the משיח. It does not include nights.

steps.title: בן זומא challenges: יציאת מצרים won't be mentioned in the days of the משיח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records בן זומא asking how יציאת מצרים could be mentioned in the days of the משיח. A פסוק in ירמיהו says people will stop mentioning it then.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: בן זומא said to the חכמים: Do we really mention יציאת מצרים in the days of the משיח? Didn't the נביא already say: 'Days are coming when people will no longer say As ה' lives Who brought Israel out of Egypt, but rather As ה' lives Who brought Israel out of the northern land and all the lands He scattered them to'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with a ברייתא in which בן זומא attacks the חכמים' reading. He quotes a פסוק that seems to say יציאת מצרים will no longer be mentioned in the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים said 'all' adds the days of the משיח, so we must mention יציאת מצרים then too. בן זומא points to ירמיהו, who says that in the future people will no longer speak about leaving Egypt. Instead they will speak about the return from all the lands of exile. If so, the חכמים' reading seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: And do we really...? (a surprised question)
The northern land, a place of exile

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a baraita:
Ben Zoma said to the Sages:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מַזְכִּירִין יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ!
phrases.english: And do we really mention the Exodus from Egypt in the days of the Messiah?!
Wasn't it already said:
"Behold, days are coming, says the Lord,

phrases.english: but rather: As the Lord lives Who brought up

phrases.english: and Who brought the seed of the house of Israel
out of the northern land and from all the lands

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the חכמים' reading from step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים' claim that 'all' adds the days of the משיח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק in ירמיהו says that in the future people will no longer mention leaving Egypt, so 'all' cannot mean we mention it then.

steps.title: יציאת מצרים stays, but becomes secondary
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that יציאת מצרים will not be wiped out. The redemption from the nations will become the main thing, and יציאת מצרים will be secondary to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: It does not mean that יציאת מצרים will be uprooted from its place. It means that being freed from the rule of the nations will be the main thing, and יציאת מצרים will be secondary to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer בן זומא's challenge by explaining the פסוק in ירמיהו differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן זומא read 'they will no longer say' as 'they will stop mentioning it completely.' The חכמים say it only means that the Exodus will no longer be the main focus. The future redemption will take first place, and the Exodus will still be mentioned in second place. So their reading of 'all' still works.

keyTerms.meaning: That it will be uprooted, removed completely
Being enslaved under the nations (the exile)

steps.whatToRemember: According to the חכמים, the future redemption will be the main thing we speak about, but יציאת מצרים will still be mentioned alongside it.

phrases.english: They said to him:
It doesn't mean that the Exodus from Egypt will be uprooted from its place,
but rather that the subjugation of the kingdoms will be primary,
phrases.notes: They mean being saved from that subjugation, the future redemption from the nations.

phrases.english: and the Exodus from Egypt will be secondary to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא שֶׁתֵּעָקֵר יְצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם מִמְּקוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers בן זומא's challenge in step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'They will no longer say' means the Exodus will not be mentioned at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They will no longer say' means it will no longer be the main focus. It will still be mentioned as secondary.

steps.title: A parallel: יעקב's name becoming ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים start bringing a similar פסוק, about יעקב's name changing to ישראל, to show that 'no longer' does not mean 'never at all.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, you say: 'Your name will no longer be called יעקב, but rather ישראל will be your name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים begin a supporting example to back up their answer. This step sets up the explanation, which continues right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק uses the same 'no longer... but rather' wording as the פסוק in ירמיהו. The name יעקב is still used after this, so 'no longer' must mean 'not as the main name.' This supports reading ירמיהו the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Similar to it, a parallel case

phrases.english: Similarly, you say:
"Your name shall no longer be called Jacob,
phrases.notes: בראשית 35:10

phrases.english: but rather Israel shall be your name,"
phrases.notes: The explanation of this פסוק continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 37 with a parallel פסוק that uses the same wording.
steps.raayaObject: That 'no longer... but rather' means primary versus secondary, not complete removal
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 35:10, the renaming of יעקב as ישראל
